title: Ameresco and Memphis Light, Gas and Water Recognized with Tennessee Governor’s Environmental Stewardship Award
summary: Ameresco and MLGW modernized more than 77,000 Memphis streetlights, strengthening reliability and public safety.
body_markdown:
## *Citywide streetlight project recognized for modernizing critical public infrastructure and strengthening reliability for the City of Memphis*


**FRAMINGHAM, MA, and MEMPHIS, TN, September 16, 2026** –[Ameresco, Inc.](http://ameresco.com/) , (NYSE: AMRC), a leading energy infrastructure company delivering integrated solutions to create reliable power and modernize infrastructure, together with[Memphis Light, Gas and Water (MLGW)](https://www.mlgw.com/) , today announced that their streetlight modernization project has been named a recipient of the 2026 Tennessee Governor’s Environmental Stewardship Award in the “Energy and Renewable Resources” category. The award, now in its 40th year, recognizes organizations for their commitment to preserving Tennessee’s natural resources.


Ameresco collaborated with MLGW, the City of Memphis, and technology provider Ubicquia to convert more than 77,000 streetlights citywide to advanced LED fixtures with connected, networked controls. The $54 million project gave MLGW a modernized system built for long-term reliability, replacing aging fixtures with infrastructure designed to keep pace with the city’s growth.


“Projects like this show what’s possible when partners work together to modernize the infrastructure people depend on every day, particularly at a large scale,” said Louis Maltezos, Co-President of Ameresco. “We’re proud to support MLGW and the City of Memphis in building a system that’s not only more reliable today, but ready to support the community’s needs well into the future.”


The project reflects both organizations’ commitment to modernizing infrastructure that supports daily life across Memphis. The upgraded system helps MLGW make better use of existing power infrastructure by reducing load, improving efficiency, and extending the value of existing assets, while giving crews real-time visibility to respond to issues faster.


That reliability extends to broader public systems, with the networked controls also giving Memphis a future-ready platform capable of supporting additional smart city technologies as needs evolve. The project is also designed to help reduce electricity consumption by more than 37,000 megawatt-hours annually, and greenhouse gas emissions by more than15,000 metric tons each year.


“This recognition reflects the strength of the partnership behind this project and what it has meant for our residents: safer streets, a more reliable system, and infrastructure built to last,” said Ursula Madden, Vice President, Corporate Communications, Memphis Light, Gas and Water. “Working with Ameresco and the City allowed us to modernize a critical public service across every neighborhood in Memphis, ensuring every community shares in these benefits.”


That impact has also earned the project national recognition, including the 2024 Smart 20 Award for Transformative City Infrastructure and commendation from the U.S. Department of Energy’s Integrated Lighting Campaign for sustainability in lighting.


To learn more about the Memphis streetlight modernization project, visit[https://www.ameresco.com/portfolio-item/city-of-memphis-tn/](https://www.ameresco.com/portfolio-item/city-of-memphis-tn/) .

**About Ameresco, Inc.**


Ameresco, Inc. (NYSE: AMRC) is a leading energy infrastructure company delivering integrated solutions to create reliable power and modernize infrastructure. The company’s *Power Infrastructure* business integrates energy resources across behind-the-meter and utility-scale systems. Its *Buildings & Public Infrastructure* business modernizes the built environment with smart, connected solutions that optimize performance and enhance resilience. Ameresco is a trusted full lifecycle partner, delivering over $15 billion in solutions and contracting over 5 GW of energy resources since its founding in 2000. Headquartered in Massachusetts, Ameresco serves public and private sector customers across North America and Europe. Learn more at[www.ameresco.com](https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.ameresco.com%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cmcahalan%40greenoughagency.com%7Cc787ad429c374400036b08dee83023ff%7C7ab732eaa60c4cbd9bcac284822be26c%7C0%7C0%7C639203490620777689%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=MxrH4NcVIQN2mSJL19BTxI7lI%2FSgn24Ft%2FUHdMD3%2Fjo%3D&reserved=0) .


Why did Ameresco and Memphis Light, Gas and Water receive the Tennessee Governor’s Environmental Stewardship Award?


Ameresco and Memphis Light, Gas and Water (MLGW) received the 2026 Tennessee Governor’s Environmental Stewardship Award in the Energy and Renewable Resources category for their citywide streetlight modernization project, which upgraded critical public infrastructure, improved system reliability, and delivered significant energy and environmental benefits across Memphis.


What is the Memphis streetlight modernization project?


Ameresco partnered with MLGW, the City of Memphis, and Ubicquia to convert more than 77,000 streetlights to advanced LED fixtures with connected, networked controls. The project modernized aging infrastructure and created a more reliable streetlighting system designed to support future community needs.


How many streetlights did Ameresco upgrade in Memphis?


Ameresco helped modernize more than 77,000 streetlights throughout Memphis. The citywide upgrade replaced aging fixtures with advanced LED technology and networked controls, creating a modern lighting system built for long-term performance and operational efficiency.


How does the Memphis streetlight project improve reliability?


Ameresco delivered a modern lighting system that provides MLGW with greater visibility into streetlight operations through connected controls. The upgraded infrastructure enables crews to identify and respond to issues more quickly while improving overall system reliability.


What are the energy savings from the Memphis LED streetlight project?


Ameresco designed the project to reduce electricity consumption by more than 37,000 megawatt-hours annually. The upgraded LED streetlights help MLGW make better use of existing power infrastructure while supporting long-term energy efficiency goals.


How does the project reduce greenhouse gas emissions?


Ameresco designed the Memphis streetlight modernization project to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by more than 15,000 metric tons each year. These reductions are expected to result from lower electricity consumption and more efficient lighting infrastructure.


How does the Memphis streetlight modernization project benefit residents?


MLGW and Ameresco modernized streetlighting infrastructure across Memphis to provide residents with a more reliable system and improved public infrastructure. The citywide deployment ensures neighborhoods throughout Memphis benefit from the upgraded lighting network.


What problem was the Memphis streetlight modernization project designed to solve?


Ameresco modernized an aging streetlight system by replacing outdated fixtures with advanced LED technology and connected controls. The project was designed to improve reliability, increase operational efficiency, reduce energy use, and strengthen critical public infrastructure.
